Many morphemes have either one takis or no takis and some have more than one takis in the underlying forms. ... According to the place of the "fall of pitch", three accent patterns are recognized. They are named "the initial accented pattern", "the middle accented pattern" and "the final accented pattern". The pattern which has no "fall of pitch" like [?ame], [?amega], etc., is named "the atonic pattern". ... new_statements.quote: アクセントは，「昇り核」（/［/）の有無と位置を語頭から数えた数字で示す。無核型は 0 とする。下北の風間浦村以外は明確な「昇り核」の方言である。 [p. 103] … ちなみに弘前方言の音調は，たとえば連体形言い切りでは，売［ルトキ］］.，［取ル］トキ. などとなる。音調型は方言により，また終止形と連体形でも異なるが，どの方言も / 売ル=/（0 型），/［取ル/（1 型）などで，アクセントは終止形も連体形も同じである。 [p. 104]
new_statements.translation: Accent is shown by the presence or absence and the position of the 'rising kernel' (/[/), as a numeral counted from the beginning of the word; the kernel-less (unaccented) type is 0. Except for Kazamaura village in Shimokita, these are clearly 'rising-kernel' dialects. [p. 103] … Incidentally, the tonal shape of the Hirosaki dialect is, for example in the sentence-final adnominal form, u[rutoki]]., [toru]toki. etc. The tonal shapes differ by dialect and also between conclusive and adnominal forms, but in every dialect it is /uru=/ (type 0), /[toru/ (type 1) etc., and the accent is the same for the conclusive and the adnominal form. [p. 104]

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for tsug1237 has an empty rule field and no existing statements; this paper supplies the type: lexical pitch accent (rising kernel), not stress. Data are from Hirosaki city (two speakers b. 1951/1952) and Goshogawara city (b. 1950), both former Tsugaru domain.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tsugaru (Hirosaki, Goshogawara) is a lexical pitch accent system of the 'rising-kernel' (noboriкaku) type: each word either has no kernel (type 0) or has a kernel whose position (counted in moras from the word start) is lexically specified; the kernel is realized as a pitch rise at that mora, with a following fall whose placement depends on the dialect and the syntactic form. No word stress is described; prominence is pitch, not stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed (none in a pitch accent system).
new_statements.exceptions: Kazamaura (Shimokita, a Nambu-han site, not Tsugaru) is a 'one-place prominence' type rather than a rising-kernel type (p. 103); the phonetic tone shape of the same kernel differs between Iwate and Hirosaki/Tsugaru (p. 104).
new_statements.identity_note: Hirayama & Sato 2003 covers Aomori Prefecture as a whole (Tsugaru and Nambu dialects). The Uwano data explicitly labelled Tsugaru-han come from Hirosaki city and Goshogawara city (2019) and Aomori city and Tsugaru city/former Shariki village (2020); Hachinohe, Kazamaura (Shimokita), Morioka and Shizukuishi in the same papers are Nambu dialect (Iwate or former Nambu domain), not Tsugaru, and Kazamaura is a different ('one-place prominence') accent type.

new_statements.quote: 全体として見ると，外来語のアクセント体系も，和語と同様，モーラ数より 1 つ多い Pn=n+1 の対立を基本とする。ただし同時に，2 モーラ語以下では無核型がなく，6 モーラ語（以上）では語頭核が極くわずかとなり，モーラ数を問わず語末核も少数派である，という制限がある。 [pp. 62-63] … ⓪：/ ○○○ =/：○○○（低平調）（岩手），○○[○（青森）。「=」は無核型の印。 ①：/[○○○ /：[○]○○ .，[○○○…（岩手）；[○○]○ .，[○○○]…（津軽） [p. 49] … These dialects exhibit n+1 contrastive pitch patterns for n-mora foreign words (3≦n≦6), with these patterns varying in accordance with the weakness of the mora structure. [English abstract, p. 69]
new_statements.translation: Seen as a whole, the accent system of foreign words too, like that of native words, is based on a Pn = n+1 contrast, one more than the number of moras. At the same time there are restrictions: words of two moras or fewer have no kernel-less type, in words of six moras (or more) word-initial kernels become extremely few, and word-final kernels are a minority whatever the mora count. [pp. 62-63] … Type 0: /○○○=/: ○○○ (low level) (Iwate), ○○[○ (Aomori); '=' marks the kernel-less type. Type 1: /[○○○/: [○]○○. , [○○○… (Iwate); [○○]○. , [○○○]… (Tsugaru). [p. 49]

new_statements.relation_note: Same conclusion as Uwano 2019: lexical pitch accent with n+1 contrast. Tsugaru data here are from Aomori city (older data, speaker b. 1935) and Tsugaru city (former Shariki village, b. 1947); the other sites (Morioka, Shizukuishi, Kazamaura) are Nambu dialect, not Tsugaru.
new_statements.rule_in_words: An n-mora word has n+1 possible contrastive pitch patterns (kernel on any mora, or no kernel); the kernel position is lexical but partly predictable from mora structure ('weak' moras — special moras and narrow-vowel moras — avoid bearing the kernel, so the kernel tends to fall on the nearest 'non-weak' mora). Prominence is a pitch rise at the kernel mora; there is no word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: No kernel-less type in words of 1-2 moras; initial kernel very rare in 6+ mora words; final-kernel type a minority; Aomori-side (Tsugaru) forms are always accented (kerneled) and place the kernel further forward than the Iwate side in several items (pp. 62-63, 'chiikisa' section).
new_statements.identity_note: Hirayama & Sato 2003 covers Aomori Prefecture as a whole (Tsugaru and Nambu dialects). The Uwano data explicitly labelled Tsugaru-han come from Hirosaki city and Goshogawara city (2019) and Aomori city and Tsugaru city/former Shariki village (2020); Hachinohe, Kazamaura (Shimokita), Morioka and Shizukuishi in the same papers are Nambu dialect (Iwate or former Nambu domain), not Tsugaru, and Kazamaura is a different ('one-place prominence') accent type.

tone_statements.citation: Uwano, Zendo (上野善道). 2020. Hokuō hōgen no dōshi no akusento shiryō (2) 北奥方言の動詞のアクセント資料(2) [Accent Data of Verbs in the Northern Tohoku Dialects: Part 2]. Kokuritsu Kokugo Kenkyūjo Ronshū (NINJAL Research Papers) 18: 35-75. doi:10.15084/00002541
tone_statements.quote: 岩手県と青森県の，旧南部・津軽両藩の6地点で調査をした北奥方言動詞のアクセント報告の続稿として，4～7拍動詞の374語を対象とする。基本は無核型と次末核型の2つからなるが，動詞の全体としてはn拍にn個の区別があるアクセント体系である。
tone_statements.translation: As a sequel to the accent report on Northern Tohoku verbs surveyed at 6 sites in Iwate and Aomori in the former Nambu and Tsugaru domains, this paper treats 374 verbs of 4-7 morae. The basis consists of two types, unaccented and penultimate-kernel, but for verbs as a whole it is an accent system with n distinctions for n morae.

tone_statements.citation: Uwano, Zendo (上野善道). 2020. Hokuō hōgen no noborikaku no yurai 北奥方言の昇り核の由来 [Where does the ascending kernel in the Northern Tohoku dialects come from?]. Kokugo Kenkyū 国語研究 (Kokugakuin University) 83: 1-26. doi:10.57529/00000957
tone_statements.quote: 津軽方言も、結論から言うと、その音韻解釈は全く雫石方言と同じで、昇り核によって弁別される Pn = n+1 の体系である。雫石方言との違いは、まず、無核型が低平調ではなく、言い切り・接続ともに文節末が高くなる。...有核型は、言い切り形が核の位置から文節次末まで高く続いて、文節末だけが下がる。...しかしながら、その下降の存在を認めたあとでも、津軽方言も共時的には「昇り核」の体系であるという解釈に何ら変わりはない。下降は義務的であっても昇り核に連動して現われるもので、下降の位置は決まっていて相互に対立をなさないからである。
tone_statements.translation: The Tsugaru dialect too, to state the conclusion first, has exactly the same phonological interpretation as the Shizukuishi dialect: it is a Pn = n+1 system distinguished by the ascending kernel. The difference from Shizukuishi is, first, that the kernel-less type is not low-level but ends high at the phrase end in both final and connective forms. ...In kernelled types the final form stays high from the kernel position to the penultimate of the phrase, and only the phrase-final mora falls. ...However, even after admitting the existence of that fall, nothing changes in the interpretation that the Tsugaru dialect is synchronically an 'ascending kernel' system: the fall, though obligatory, appears linked to the ascending kernel, its position is fixed, and the two do not contrast with each other.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 7-8, sec. 2.2 津軽方言, after table (5)
tone_statements.summary: N. Tohoku-type word-pitch accent: an n-mora word has n+1 accent classes, set by presence and position of an 'ascending kernel' (rise onto the kernel mora); the obligatory later fall is non-distinctive, per the author a relic of an old lowering kernel. Noun paradigm table (Aomori/Hirosaki). No stress.

tone_statements.citation: Takayama, Rintarō (高山林太郎), Kōhei Nakazawa (中澤光平) and Tomoyo Ōtsuki (大槻知世). 2012. A1-4. 青森市若年層のアクセントについて: ダウンステップ, 低平化, 高平化 (研究発表, 日本音声学会2012年度(第26回)全国大会発表要旨) [On the accent of young speakers in Aomori City: downstep, low-levelling, high-levelling]. Onsei Kenkyū 音声研究 16(3): 100. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.16.3_100_1
tone_statements.quote: 青森市方言のアクセント体系では，「そこで昇ろうとする力」である昇り核の有無と位置が弁別的である（上野 1984 など）。…本発表の目的は，津軽方言のダウンステップの条件等について更に細かく検討することである。調査方法は，青森市出身の 20 代女性を対象として，単語，短文を読み上げる形式で行った。その結果，以下のことが明らかになった。有核語が先行する場合にダウンステップが生じるが，先行語の核の位置によるダウンステップの効果には特に大きな差は見られない。
tone_statements.translation: In the accent system of the Aomori City dialect, the presence/absence and position of the ascending kernel, 'the force to rise at that point', are distinctive (Uwano 1984 etc.). ... The aim of this presentation is to examine in more detail the conditions on downstep in the Tsugaru dialect. The survey had a woman in her 20s from Aomori City read aloud words and short sentences. The following became clear. Downstep occurs when a kernel-bearing word precedes, but the position of the preceding word's kernel makes no particular large difference to the downstep effect.
tone_statements.summary: Ascending-kernel pitch accent system (kernel presence and position distinctive, after Uwano 1984); the abstract finds downstep after accented words, plus low-levelling (低平調) and high-levelling (高平調) phrase patterns. Pitch as levels 5-1 per mora (黒い布 155・14). No accent-class count; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Kobayashi, Yasuhide (小林泰秀). 1985. Hirosaki hōgen no onchō merodē 弘前方言の音調メロデー [The Tone Melody of the Hirosaki Dialect]. Gengo Kenkyu (Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 87: 40-67. doi:10.11435/gengo1939.1985.40
tone_statements.quote: The basic tone melody of the Hirosaki Dialect is LH (Low-High) and all syllables become high-toned before a phrase boundary if followed by another phrase. ... we cannot say that there is a falling of tone after an accented syllable, but we rather say that there is a rising of tone before an accented syllable.

tone.translation: As a sequel to the accent report on Northern Tohoku verbs surveyed at 6 sites in Iwate and Aomori in the former Nambu and Tsugaru domains, this paper treats 374 verbs of 4-7 morae. The basis consists of two types, unaccented and penultimate-kernel, but for verbs as a whole it is an accent system with n distinctions for n morae.
tone.says: Accent data for 374 verbs of 4-7 morae at six Northern Tohoku sites (former Tsugaru and Nambu domains): the basic verb types are unaccented (無核型) and penultimate-kernel (次末核型), but over the verb lexicon as a whole the system distinguishes n accent classes for n morae; accent of 8 conjugational forms for 35 basic verbs up to 3 morae, with regional differences noted.

sources.citation: Uwano, Zendo (上野善道). 2020. Hokuō hōgen no noborikaku no yurai 北奥方言の昇り核の由来 [Where does the ascending kernel in the Northern Tohoku dialects come from?]. Kokugo Kenkyū 国語研究 (Kokugakuin University) 83: 1-26. doi:10.57529/00000957
sources.quote: 津軽方言も、結論から言うと、その音韻解釈は全く雫石方言と同じで、昇り核によって弁別される Pn = n+1 の体系である。雫石方言との違いは、まず、無核型が低平調ではなく、言い切り・接続ともに文節末が高くなる。...有核型は、言い切り形が核の位置から文節次末まで高く続いて、文節末だけが下がる。...しかしながら、その下降の存在を認めたあとでも、津軽方言も共時的には「昇り核」の体系であるという解釈に何ら変わりはない。下降は義務的であっても昇り核に連動して現われるもので、下降の位置は決まっていて相互に対立をなさないからである。

Noun paradigm table (Aomori/Hirosaki). No stress.

tone.translation: The Tsugaru dialect too, to state the conclusion first, has exactly the same phonological interpretation as the Shizukuishi dialect: it is a Pn = n+1 system distinguished by the ascending kernel. The difference from Shizukuishi is, first, that the kernel-less type is not low-level but ends high at the phrase end in both final and connective forms. ...In kernelled types the final form stays high from the kernel position to the penultimate of the phrase, and only the phrase-final mora falls. ...However, even after admitting the existence of that fall, nothing changes in the interpretation that the Tsugaru dialect is synchronically an 'ascending kernel' system: the fall, though obligatory, appears linked to the ascending kernel, its position is fixed, and the two do not contrast with each other.

Noun paradigm table (Aomori/Hirosaki). No stress.

sources.citation: Takayama, Rintarō (高山林太郎), Kōhei Nakazawa (中澤光平) and Tomoyo Ōtsuki (大槻知世). 2012. A1-4. 青森市若年層のアクセントについて: ダウンステップ, 低平化, 高平化 (研究発表, 日本音声学会2012年度(第26回)全国大会発表要旨) [On the accent of young speakers in Aomori City: downstep, low-levelling, high-levelling]. Onsei Kenkyū 音声研究 16(3): 100. doi:10.24467/onseikenkyu.16.3_100_1
sources.quote: 青森市方言のアクセント体系では，「そこで昇ろうとする力」である昇り核の有無と位置が弁別的である（上野 1984 など）。…本発表の目的は，津軽方言のダウンステップの条件等について更に細かく検討することである。調査方法は，青森市出身の 20 代女性を対象として，単語，短文を読み上げる形式で行った。その結果，以下のことが明らかになった。有核語が先行する場合にダウンステップが生じるが，先行語の核の位置によるダウンステップの効果には特に大きな差は見られない。
sources.note: Ascending-kernel pitch accent system (kernel presence and position distinctive, after Uwano 1984); the abstract finds downstep after accented words, plus low-levelling (低平調) and high-levelling (高平調) phrase patterns. Pitch as levels 5-1 per mora (黒い布 155・14). No accent-class count; nothing on stress.

tone.quote: 青森市方言のアクセント体系では，「そこで昇ろうとする力」である昇り核の有無と位置が弁別的である（上野 1984 など）。…本発表の目的は，津軽方言のダウンステップの条件等について更に細かく検討することである。調査方法は，青森市出身の 20 代女性を対象として，単語，短文を読み上げる形式で行った。その結果，以下のことが明らかになった。有核語が先行する場合にダウンステップが生じるが，先行語の核の位置によるダウンステップの効果には特に大きな差は見られない。
tone.translation: In the accent system of the Aomori City dialect, the presence/absence and position of the ascending kernel, 'the force to rise at that point', are distinctive (Uwano 1984 etc.). ... The aim of this presentation is to examine in more detail the conditions on downstep in the Tsugaru dialect. The survey had a woman in her 20s from Aomori City read aloud words and short sentences. The following became clear. Downstep occurs when a kernel-bearing word precedes, but the position of the preceding word's kernel makes no particular large difference to the downstep effect.
tone.summary: Ascending-kernel pitch accent system (kernel presence and position distinctive, after Uwano 1984); the abstract finds downstep after accented words, plus low-levelling (低平調) and high-levelling (高平調) phrase patterns. Pitch as levels 5-1 per mora (黒い布 155・14). No accent-class count; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kobayashi, Yasuhide (小林泰秀). 1985. Hirosaki hōgen no onchō merodē 弘前方言の音調メロデー [The Tone Melody of the Hirosaki Dialect]. Gengo Kenkyu (Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 87: 40-67. doi:10.11435/gengo1939.1985.40
sources.quote: The basic tone melody of the Hirosaki Dialect is LH (Low-High) and all syllables become high-toned before a phrase boundary if followed by another phrase. ... we cannot say that there is a falling of tone after an accented syllable, but we rather say that there is a rising of tone before an accented syllable.

sources.note: Autosegmental tonology of Hirosaki (Tsugaru) accent: basic tone melody is LH (opposite of Tokyo HL); all syllables become H before a phrase boundary when another phrase follows; the fall is predictable, so the system is analysed as a rise before the accented syllable (ascending accent) rather than a fall after it; tone association rules and their domain differ from Tokyo; three accent-shift rules (final accent moves onto certain enclitics; accented consonant-stem verb + -ta/-te shifts accent to the suffix; word-initial accent moves to the second syllable with a non-high vowel); downdrift deri…

No pitch shapes, no count of accent classes, nothing on stress. p. 68 has 78 forms.

tone.quote: 拙稿(2006)に引き続き，青森市方言の後部要素が2拍からなる複合名詞のアクセント規則を解明するための資料を提示する。2回目の今回は，後部要素がサ行の場合を扱う。... 資料の形式も変わりない。後部要素の読みの順で，同一要素の中は，複合語全体のアクセントの 0,-1,-2,…の順（0 は無核，-1 以降は昇り核の位置を後ろから数えた数字)，同じアクセントの中では前部要素の読みの五十音順とした。
tone.translation: Continuing from my earlier paper (2006), I present data for clarifying the accent rules of compound nouns of the Aomori City dialect whose final member consists of 2 moras. This second instalment treats final members beginning with the sa-row. ... The format of the data is also unchanged. Entries follow the reading order of the final member; within the same member, the order of the accent of the whole compound, 0, -1, -2, ... (0 is kernel-less; -1 onwards is the number giving the position of the ascending kernel counted from the end), and within the same accent, the kana order of the first member's reading.
